_comment: Rate limits as DATA, not prose, so correcting one is a one-line pull request.
Every entry carries how we know it. The values of `confidence` are not decoration:
MEASURED  - we saw it ourselves: a response header, a usage endpoint, or a 429 we walked into.
`measured_on` says when.
DECLARED  - the provider says so on a page we read. `source` and `read_on` say where and when.
DERIVED   - arithmetic on figures the provider publishes, with the arithmetic shown. A daily
token figure computed from a request cap is DERIVED, never DECLARED, because the
provider published the requests and we chose the tokens per reply.
PAID-PLAN - the only published number belongs to a PAID tier, not the free one. Publishing it
as a free-tier figure is the mistake this repo calls out in its own README. A row
whose only daily figure is PAID-PLAN is not ranked and enters no sum.
UNKNOWN   - nobody publishes it and we have not measured it. This stays UNKNOWN. We do not guess,
and we do not copy a number out of another list to fill the hole.
`scope` is the field most lists omit and it changes everything: a limit that applies per ORGANIZATION
or per PROJECT does not get bigger when you make another key.
`volatile: true` means this number moved under us at least once, or the provider stopped publishing it.
Re-measure before quoting it.
ONE SHAPE FOR THE PER-MINUTE CEILING: every provider has `all_models` with rpm / tpm / tpm_input /
tpm_output at provider level. Where the provider publishes per-model figures they stay under
`models` for detail, and `all_models` carries the largest of them with a `note` saying so.
THREE KINDS OF FREE, AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME SHELF:
RECURRING  what you get every day, forever. This is what `all_models` and `models` describe.
MONTHLY    a pot that refreshes each month: credits in money or tokens. It lives in `monthly`.
ONE-TIME   a bundle handed over once at sign-up: a pot of tokens, or credits in money. Real
on day one, gone on day two. It lives in `one_time` and is NEVER added to the
daily figure - every list that adds them together is quoting a number that stops
being true after 24 hours.
A grant in MONEY is not converted into tokens unless the provider publishes a price we read
ourselves. $5 of credits is $5 of credits until then.
Nothing in this file describes an account. What an endpoint did is recorded as the HTTP code it
returned and the date it returned it; what a meter read at that moment is not recorded.

groq.scope_quote: Rate limits apply at the organization level, not individual users.
groq.caveat: The published table is labelled as the BASE LIMITS OF THE DEVELOPER PLAN, not the free tier. Quote: 'the limits shown below are the base limits for the Developer plan'. Free-tier values are not published; check your own console at /settings/limits. Every list that reprints 1,000 requests/day as a free-tier figure is reprinting a paid plan's number.

all_models.note: per model; the largest is shown

groq.binding_limit: TPM, not RPD. 8,000 tokens per minute is what you actually hit: a long prompt returns 413 long before you approach 1,000 requests. We measured that 413 on an article-length prompt.

measured.note: Rate-limit response headers read on 2026-09-07 reported x-ratelimit-limit-requests 1000 per day and x-ratelimit-limit-tokens 8000 per minute, the same figures as the published Developer-plan table. Whether those headers describe the free tier or a trial is not published anywhere we could find, so the daily figure keeps the PAID-PLAN label and the row is not ranked on it. The per-minute token ceiling is what actually stops you: a long prompt returns HTTP 413 long before the request count matters.

cerebras.measured_how: rate-limit response headers on a free-trial key, read 2026-09-02 and again 2026-09-07: x-ratelimit-limit-requests-day 2400, x-ratelimit-limit-tokens-day 1000000, 5 requests/minute. The figures held across five days.
cerebras.caveat: Their pricing page on 2026-09-06 describes free access only as 'Free Trial: $5 in free credits after making an account' and publishes no daily free-tier ceiling at all. The numbers below are what the response headers of a free-trial key reported between 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-07. They may be trial allowance rather than a standing free tier. Re-measure before relying on them.
cerebras.binding_limit: 5 requests per minute. Two calls inside the same minute need roughly 13 s between them.

one_time.quote: Free Trial: $5 in free credits after making an account
one_time.note: Their pricing page describes free access ONLY as this trial and publishes no daily free-tier ceiling. The 1,000,000 tokens/day above came from the response headers of a free-trial key and may be this trial rather than a standing tier.

google.caveat: The public docs page no longer prints the per-model table; it points you at aistudio.google.com/rate-limit, which needs a login. The figures below were read off that console screen on 2026-09-06. Free tier means literally 'no billing account linked': linking one moves the project to Tier 1 and off these numbers. Because the limits are per PROJECT, a second API key in the same project buys you nothing.

gemini-3.8-flash.note: The console screen read on 2026-09-06 showed 20 requests a day for 3.7 Flash and no row for 3.8 Flash, so no daily figure is recorded here. The 5/min WAS measured: a sixth call inside six seconds returned HTTP 429 with 'limit: 5'.
gemini-3.8-flash.measured_how: a sixth call inside six seconds returned HTTP 429 with 'limit: 5' in the body; recorded in this file on 2026-09-06
gemini-3.8-flash.unknown_reason: the 20 requests a day on the screen read 2026-09-06 belonged to gemini-3.7-flash; no daily figure for gemini-3.8-flash has been read

gemma-4-31b-it.note: Not published on the screen we read, and not measured.

all_models.note: per model; the largest is shown

google.binding_limit: Requests per DAY on the Flash models: 500 a day on 3.5 Flash-Lite, and no daily figure has been read for 3.8 Flash.

openrouter.caveat: The daily cap depends on lifetime credits purchased, and applies across ALL :free models combined, not per model. This condition is the one most lists drop, which makes their number wrong for a new account by a factor of twenty.

all_models.note: rpd is tiered by lifetime credits purchased: see free_models_combined

measured.note: 431 models listed on the public /models endpoint, of which 19 end in :free (4.4%)

cloudflare.caveat: Cloudflare bills in Neurons, not tokens, and publishes both the free allocation and the conversion on the same page. 10,000 Neurons a day divided by 34,868 Neurons per million output tokens is about 286,795 output tokens a day on llama-3.1-8b: their two numbers, our division, so it is marked DERIVED and never counted as measured. Every model has its own Neuron price, and llama-3.3-70b costs six times more per output token than the 8b model, so that figure belongs to the model it was computed on: a tracked model gets a DERIVED figure only from its own price in neuron_cost_examples, and a tracked model whose price is not on file has an UNKNOWN daily volume rather than another model's number. Seven models are excluded from the free tier entirely and need a paid billing method.
quotes: Our free allocation allows anyone to use a total of 10,000 Neurons per day at no charge.
All limits reset daily at 00:00 UTC.
@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fp8-fast | 4119 neurons per M input tokens, 34868 neurons per M output tokens
Text Generation | 300 requests per minute
cloudflare.binding_limit: Neurons per day, at 10,000. On a small text model that is roughly a quarter of a million output tokens; on a large one, far fewer.

signup_requires.note: Email and password only, per their account-creation guide.

nvidia.caveat: We carried a figure of 40 requests per minute per key in our own notes, but we could not find it on a public NVIDIA page when we went looking, so it is NOT published here as a rate limit. Unknown, not 40. What we do have is our own concurrency measurement below, which is worth more anyway: it says how many calls the model takes in parallel, which no rate-limit table tells you. If you find the published figure, the source URL is a one-line pull request.

measured_concurrency.moonshotai/kimi-k3: serial only: 7 of 8 concurrent calls returned 429 instantly. 25-55 s per call, so roughly 60-100 per hour if nothing else shares the key.

ollama.caveat: A monthly starter allowance whose size they do not publish, one concurrent request, and no roll-over. That is the whole of what is knowable from their own pages.
ollama.concurrency: assume 1 - concurrent execution is sold as a paid-plan feature

monthly.quote: Free accounts include a starter amount of usage for a smaller set of starter models. Instead, your included amount refreshes at each monthly reset.
monthly.note: They say a starter allowance exists, that it refreshes monthly, and not how big it is. That is exactly what this row records: a monthly grant of unpublished size.

quotes: Free accounts include a starter amount of usage for a smaller set of starter models.
Free includes 1 concurrent request
Instead, your included amount refreshes at each monthly reset.
ollama.binding_limit: One request at a time, and a monthly allowance nobody outside Ollama can size.

alibaba.caveat: Two different things, and lists confuse them constantly. The 1,000,000 tokens per model is a ONE-TIME grant that expires in 90 days. The rate limits below are RECURRING and apply while that grant lasts: their page states the same RPM and TPM apply to free-quota users as to paying ones. There is no cumulative daily cap; the ceiling is per minute.

all_models.note: per model; the largest is shown

one_time.quote: Each model (such as qwen-plus, qwen3.6-plus, or qwen3.6-plus-2026-04-02) has its own independent free quota (typically 1,000,000 tokens). Quota cannot be merged or transferred across models.
one_time.expires_quote: The free quota is valid for 90 days, starting from the date you activate Alibaba Cloud Model Studio, the model is released, or your model request is approved (whichever is later).
one_time.note: 1,000,000 tokens PER MODEL, their rule, quoted above: the quotas are independent and cannot be merged. Recorded per model rather than multiplied by the number of models this list happens to track, because that product would move when this list adds a model, not when Alibaba changes its grant. Singapore region only, and calls stop when the quota is exhausted unless account details are completed, at which point usage is billed.

alibaba.tpm_note: 5,000,000 is the ceiling on qwen-flash and qwen-turbo, and it counts input AND output together - their sentence, not our reading. qwen-plus is 1,000,000.
alibaba.binding_limit: Tokens per minute, at 5,000,000 on the flash models - and, underneath it, the one-time grant running out.

signup_requires.note: Account verification requires a mobile number.

xkiro.measured_how: their own usage endpoint, GET /v1/usage on the API host, which reports the daily token allowance
xkiro.caveat: The largest confirmed free token allowance in this list by a wide margin, and it took one GET to find - it was sitting behind an endpoint nobody had asked. Requests per day are NOT published; the ceiling here is tokens.
xkiro.binding_limit: Tokens, not requests. 5M/day is roughly 3,500 pages of output, so on this provider you will hit model quality or latency long before you hit the quota.

siliconflow.caveat: The daily cap they publish applies to unverified accounts on two specific models, and everything else is per minute. The quotes on file do not name the two models, so whether Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct is one of them is not established: the daily figure is UNKNOWN until the page is re-read with the model names. On 2026-09-07 the chat endpoint answered HTTP 402 Payment Required: the $1 is a one-time grant, and a 402 is what this endpoint returns once a grant no longer covers the call.

all_models.note: rpd is null on purpose: see unverified_accounts.

unverified_accounts.applies_to: two specific models on unverified accounts; the model names are not in the quotes on file, so this is not applied to the tracked model

one_time.quote: Flexible token pricing, high usage limits, and postpaid billing - plus $1 in free credits to get you started!
one_time.note: One dollar, in money, not tokens. We do not convert it: that needs their per-token price and a made-up conversion is a confident wrong number. On 2026-09-07 the chat endpoint answered HTTP 402 Payment Required, which is how a one-time grant looks from the outside after it ends: the endpoint stops serving until a top-up.

quotes: Limit: 100 requests/day
30 requests/hour
siliconflow.binding_limit: Tokens per minute, at 40,000, and the one-time dollar underneath it. A daily cap of 100 requests exists for two models on unverified accounts; whether the tracked model is one of them is not established.

uncloseai.caveat: A keyless endpoint that publishes a limit is rare enough to be worth saying out loud: 3 requests per second per client IP, and a 65,536-token context. No account, no key, no card.
uncloseai.binding_limit: Three requests a second, per IP.
quotes: 3 requests per second, per client IP

ovhcloud.measured_how: Response headers on an anonymous POST: ratelimit-limit 2, x-ratelimit-limit-minute 2, the per-minute allowance header at 0, ratelimit-reset 44. Two attempts 90 seconds apart, both HTTP 429, both showing 0 left in the minute: the anonymous bucket is shared with every caller and was already empty both times.
ovhcloud.caveat: 2 requests a minute is the anonymous tier and it is what a reader without an account gets. The authenticated tier is 400 a minute but needs a Public Cloud project with a payment method on file, so it is not a free tier. No daily or monthly cap is published for either.
ovhcloud.binding_limit: Requests per minute, at 2, shared with everyone. This is what a free tier with no sign-up actually costs: you are queueing behind the whole internet.
quotes: Anonymous: 2 requests per minute, per IP and per model
the AI Endpoints platform does not impose any usage limits for API requests, apart from the rate and payload size limiting

authenticated_tier.why: requires a Public Cloud project with a payment method

signup_requires.note: The anonymous tier needs nothing; the 400/min tier needs a Public Cloud project with a payment method.

mistral.measured_how: Their own rate-limit headers, read seven times on 2026-09-07. The ceiling the headers report MOVES, and not slowly: at 00:05 UTC they said x-ratelimit-limit-tokens-minute 625000 and the call returned a completion. Five readings between 00:39 and 00:43 UTC, one minute apart, all said x-ratelimit-limit-req-minute 0 and every call was refused with HTTP 429. Earlier the same day the headers had also said 0.
mistral.caveat: Their pricing page answers what the header readings could not: the Free plan grants $10 a month in API credits. That is why the ceiling read 625,000 tokens a minute once and zero six times within an hour: a monthly pot, not a standing rate. A limit header of zero with HTTP 429 on every call is what that pot looks like from the outside for the rest of the month, not the tier being switched off. No token figure is published, so none is recorded here; the credit is in monthly.
mistral.binding_limit: Ten dollars a month of credits, and no published conversion into tokens.

monthly.note: Ten dollars a month, in money. Not converted into tokens: no per-token price for the free plan is published.

kenari.measured_how: response headers on a call made 2026-09-07: x-ratelimit-limit 5, with a reset timestamp. The unit is not stated in the header name.
kenari.caveat: Three tiers by account status. A new account is Solo: 50 free-model requests a day and 5 a minute. A top-up of Rp 10,000 moves it to Payer, at 1,000 a day. The header measured on 2026-09-07 read x-ratelimit-limit 5, which matches the Solo per-minute figure.
kenari.binding_limit: Fifty free requests a day until a top-up moves the account to Payer.
quotes: Free-model requests per day, Solo: 50
Free-model requests per minute: 5
Free-model requests per day, Payer: 1000

signup_requires.note: Indonesian gateway; top-up is optional and moves you up a tier.

aihubmix.caveat: The generous number costs one dollar. A new account gets 10 trial calls and nothing else; a single top-up of $1 switches the account permanently to daily quotas. So the 1,000,000 tokens a day is real, recurring and unlimited in time - but it is not free until you have paid a dollar once, and this row says so rather than printing the big number on its own.
aihubmix.binding_limit: Requests per day, at 100, long before the million tokens.

unlock.quote: Every account starts with 10 trial calls, no credit card, and a $1 top-up switches you to permanent daily quotas.

quotes: All free models share one pool of 1M tokens per day.
Any top-up of $1 or more permanently switches your account to daily quotas: 10 requests per minute, 100 requests per day and 1M tokens per day, shared across all free models.
No trial expiry. Free models remain available within their respective per-minute and daily quotas indefinitely.
All 56 models bill $0 for input and output tokens.

signup_requires.note: 10 trial calls with no credit card; $1 unlocks the daily quotas.

inferx.caveat: Their Free plan is $0 a month and the free models bill $0 per million tokens in and out. No request limit, no token limit and no concurrency figure is published anywhere we could find, which is its own kind of answer.
inferx.binding_limit: Unknown. They publish a price of zero and no ceiling at all.
quotes: $0 / month
Input pricing $0.07, shown struck through, $0 / 1M Free - 100% off

unorouter.caveat: Their free models are metered as a WAITING WINDOW, not a daily allowance: roughly one request per minute per free model, and a request may be at most 8,000 tokens. No daily token budget, no tokens-per-minute figure and no concurrency figure is published.
unorouter.binding_limit: One request a minute, per free model.
quotes: About 1 request per minute per free model
Max size: 8000 tokens

hetzner.quote: As long as the Inference API remains in experimental status, it is free of charge.
hetzner.caveat: Their limits table publishes ONE timeframe, 60 seconds, and no daily row: 4M input tokens, 100k output tokens, 10 requests. Read from the page's raw HTML on 2026-09-07 because lists elsewhere quote a 24-hour row of 500M input and 5M output that is not on the page. Free only while the service stays experimental, and they say they will email before that changes. On 2026-09-07 the three instruments disagreed within the same day, which is the fact worth recording: the 30-second burst got 503 'failed to find endpoint candidates for serving the request' from both models, while the 60-minute draw at the published 10 requests a minute received 333 replies from Qwen3.8-27B. Capacity here comes and goes inside a day, so the published ceiling is generous and no single instrument is a day.
hetzner.binding_limit: Output tokens per minute, at 100,000 - and, today, whether any capacity answers at all.

signup_requires.note: Two ways to verify an account: an ID document or a payment method. A phone number is optional at creation.
